description: Shared parameter schema for the browser and generate.py. One JSON object reproduces one model.

presetNotes.Classic Gyroid: Even cells, no warp. The reference for every other preset.
presetNotes.Dense: Short period. More cells inside the same cube.
presetNotes.Open: Long period. Only a few cells, large openings.
presetNotes.Vertical Stretch: Cells pulled taller than they are wide.
presetNotes.Horizontal Stretch: Cells pulled wider than they are tall.
presetNotes.Strong Twist: The field rotates with height. The cube does not.
presetNotes.Curved: The field bends inside the fixed cube.
presetNotes.Tapered: Smaller cells at the bottom, larger cells at the top.
presetNotes.Density Gradient: The pattern opens gradually toward the top.
presetNotes.Organic: Phase, wave, bulge, and sine-noise together.
presetNotes.Extreme: Experimental. Several warps at once. Export may fail validation.

ui.label: Model
ui.note: The cube is a clipping window. The solid you see is the sheet, cut off on the six faces. There is no outer box skin.

controls.label: Family
controls.help: Which implicit equation is evaluated. Gyroid is a balanced labyrinth. Diamond is more triangular. Primitive is a softer network of holes.

controls.label: Size X
controls.help: Width of the clipping cube. The pattern is cut at this plane; a wall is not built here.

controls.label: Size Y
controls.help: Depth of the clipping cube.

controls.label: Size Z
controls.help: Height of the clipping cube. The finished mesh sits on z = 0.

controls.label: Period X
controls.help: Cell size along X. Smaller values repeat the pattern more densely. Independent of Y and Z, so cells can be stretched.

controls.label: Period Y
controls.help: Cell size along Y.

controls.label: Period Z
controls.help: Cell size along Z. Raise this alone to stretch the cells vertically.

controls.label: Level Offset
controls.help: Moves the sheet off the zero level of the equation. It changes the balance of the two labyrinths. Extreme values can pinch a channel shut or disconnect the sheet.

controls.label: Wall Thickness
controls.help: Requested physical thickness of the sheet. The equation uses a separate number, t, which is calibrated against a measurement. The hard floor is 1.2 mm.

controls.label: Phase X
controls.help: Slides the pattern through the cube along X. The cube stays still. 360 degrees is one full cell.

controls.label: Phase Y
controls.help: Slides the pattern along Y.

controls.label: Phase Z
controls.help: Slides the pattern along Z.

controls.label: Twist Mode
controls.help: Rotates the coordinate field around height before the equation is evaluated. Off leaves it straight.

controls.label: Twist Rate
controls.help: Degrees of rotation per millimetre of height. At 1 deg/mm, an 80 mm cube twists 80 degrees from bottom to top.

controls.label: Twist Strength
controls.help: Total twist, in degrees, reached at the top of the cube when the mode is nonlinear.

controls.label: Twist Exponent
controls.help: 1 spreads the twist evenly. Greater than 1 holds it back until near the top.

controls.label: Bend X
controls.help: Bends the field in X as height changes. The clipping cube stays rectangular.

controls.label: Bend Y
controls.help: Bends the field in Y as height changes.

controls.label: Bend Exponent
controls.help: 1 is a steady lean. 2 is a parabolic bow.

controls.label: Density Gradient
controls.help: Varies the period across the cube so one region is denser than another. Radial is measured from the vertical centre line.

controls.label: Gradient Strength
controls.help: Positive opens the cells along the gradient. Negative tightens them. 0 is uniform.

controls.label: Gradient Exponent
controls.help: 1 is a steady change. Higher values push the change toward one end.

controls.label: Taper X
controls.help: Changes the X cell size from bottom to top. Positive means smaller cells at the bottom and larger cells at the top.

controls.label: Taper Y
controls.help: Same transition along Y.

controls.label: Bulge Strength
controls.help: Expands or compresses the field around one height. Positive stretches the cells there. Negative packs them.

controls.label: Bulge Radius
controls.help: Width of the bulge region.

controls.label: Bulge Height
controls.help: Where the bulge sits. 0 is the bottom, 1 is the top.

controls.label: Wave Amplitude
controls.help: How far a sine wave pushes the coordinates.

controls.label: Wave Frequency
controls.help: How many waves fit along the axis.

controls.label: Wave Axis
controls.help: Which coordinate the wave pushes.

controls.label: Noise Strength
controls.help: How far deterministic sine-noise displaces the field. It is not a random texture, and it needs no extra library.

controls.label: Noise Scale
controls.help: Size of the wobble. Larger is a broader, slower disturbance.

controls.label: Noise Seed
controls.help: Picks a different sine pattern. The same seed always rebuilds the same shape.

controls.label: Thickness Mode
controls.help: Constant uses one wall. The other modes vary thickness in space. The field is clamped so the request never goes below 1.2 mm.

controls.label: Thickness Start
controls.help: Thickness at the bottom (Z mode) or at the centre (radial mode).

controls.label: Thickness End
controls.help: Thickness at the top (Z mode) or toward the sides (radial mode).

controls.label: Thickness Wave
controls.help: Added and subtracted from the requested wall along height. Anything under 1.2 mm is lifted back to 1.2.

controls.label: Thickness Wave Frequency
controls.help: How many thickness waves fit in the height.

controls.label: Rotate X
controls.help: Turns the field coordinates about the cube centre. The clipping cube does not rotate.

controls.label: Rotate Y
controls.help: Turns the field about Y.

controls.label: Rotate Z
controls.help: Turns the field about Z.

controls.label: Mirror X
controls.help: Reflects the field across the middle of the cube on X.

controls.label: Mirror Y
controls.help: Reflects the field across the middle of the cube on Y.

controls.label: Mirror Z
controls.help: Reflects the field across the mid-height of the cube.

ui.label: Quality
ui.note: The viewport uses the preview grid. The printable STL uses the final grid, then thickness calibration and an independent check. 320³ is about a gigabyte of working memory. 384³ can be several gigabytes and a very large file.

controls.label: Preview Resolution
controls.help: Grid for the on-screen mesh. While a slider is moving, the view drops lower and rebuilds when you release it.

controls.label: Final Resolution
controls.help: Grid for the STL. Default 320. A wall of 1.6 mm then spans about 6 voxels. Lower grids are faster and less trustworthy for thickness.

controls.label: Field Smooth
controls.help: Optional blur of the field, in voxels, before the surface is extracted. 0 leaves the cube cut sharp. Above 0 rounds that cut and can thin the wall after it was measured.

controls.label: Mesh Smooth
controls.help: Optional smoothing of the mesh after extraction. 0 is off. Turning it up softens the clipped faces.
